title: Focusing of dead <area>s is wonky and non-compliant in browsers.

labels.name: needs tests
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires someone to write tests

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The [spec for the <area> element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/image-maps.html#the-area-element) says:
> The [area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/image-maps.html#the-area-element) element [represents](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#represents) either a hyperlink with some text and a corresponding area on an [image map](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/image-maps.html#image-map), or a dead area on an image map.

and also
> If the [area](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/image-maps.html#the-area-element) element has no [href](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/links.html#attr-hyperlink-href) attribute, then the area represented by the element cannot be selected

However, when you actually create a dead <area> (one without `href`), Firefox still allows navigating to its clickable region via the keyboard and both it and Chrome still process click events on the region just fine.
The only thing they both agree on is that a dead <area> should not show a pointer cursor on hover. (although this can be changed with CSS)

Given that click events still work, and dead areas seem like a useful thing (I used them as buttons today), I feel like the safest path to interop here might just be to allow them and remove the part about them not being selectable from the spec.
